title: Digital circadian biomarkers of bipolar disorders
summary:
Bipolar disorders are a mental illness where people experience recurring episodes of mania and depression. Treatment remains challenging, as many patients continue to have recurring illness episodes despite standard therapy.

The medication lithium is considered the gold standard for prophylactic treatment, but its use is complicated due to potential side effects and the need for careful, time-consuming dosing. Disturbances in the circadian rhythm (the body's internal 24-hour clock) are a central element in the development of bipolar disorders. It is also known that lithium influences the circadian rhythm.

Early studies suggest that patients who respond well to lithium show early, lithium-induced changes in their circadian rhythm, whereas these changes are absent or less pronounced in non-responders. Continuously measuring the circadian rhythm has been methodologically challenging (e.g. through continuous actigraphy).

In the present study, the researchers aim to use the participant's own smartphone as a low-threshold and potentially scalable data source to derive circadian parameters. Bipolar patients newly treated with lithium will be monitored using smartphone sensor data as well as established methods (actigraphy, home sleep EEG) to investigate whether early changes in the circadian rhythm occur in lithium responders and whether these can be reliably captured using the smartphone.

The study concept has high translational potential with relevant clinical utility, also for other areas where circadian rhythm assessment is relevant. The primary goal of this exploratory study is to examine whether smartphone-based measures of the circadian rhythm change in the early phase after the start of lithium treatment, and whether these early changes are associated with clinical response to lithium after six months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosis of a bipolar disorder (type I or II), confirmed by a structured clinical interview (MINI)
• Euthymia in the past 3 months (anamnestic, as well as current YMRS ≤12, MADRS ≤12) 
• Planned initiation (or re-initiation) of lithium treatment by the treating psychiatrist. For re-initiation, the lithium-free interval should be at least 6 months
• Age: 18-50 years
• Regular, daily smartphone usage
• Capacity to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute affective episode (MADRS > 12 or YMRS >12) requiring immediate treatment adjustment or inpatient treatment
• Working in shift work (night shifts, rotating shifts, etc.)
• Severe comorbid conditions:
o Current substance dependence (e.g., consumption ≥ 3 days/week) requiring detoxification
o Serious physical illness (unstable cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, uncontrolled thyroid disorders, sleep apnea) that would have a significant influence on the circadian rhythm or lithium metabolism
• Cognitive impairment: Lack of understanding of the study procedures, questionnaires or informed consent
• Planned changes in psychotropic medication: Planned significant change (≥ 50% change in daily dose) in another psychotropic medication, e.g. antipsychotics, during study participation
